messages:
maria: heads-up — noticed p99 is drifting up in eu-west1 since 03:00 UTC, correlates with a flappy ToR in rack-12. p95 mostly fine. wondering if we should tighten admit curve or rely on regional fallback?

alex: ugh, that ToR has been noisy. how much headroom do we currently keep for eu-west1 during peaks?

leo: current config: target p99 600ms, p95 150ms. soft admit keeps 20% headroom, hard admit at 35%. we sized for steady-state load, not intermittent network-induced tail.

maria: observed traffic multiplier x1.3 for a 15m window; queue depth spiked and KV cache churned. GPUs stayed at 70% but latency hit token-steady tail.

ops-bot: deploy-check: no recent model roll or runtime change in eu-west1 in last 6h.

jamie: quick math thought — if network flapping adds an extra 80ms median RPC and 200ms tail for some fraction f of requests, effective p99 grows. we can either: reduce admitted concurrency by factor c or route a fraction r to other regions (cost + egress).

priya: can you sketch the admit math? need something we can test in the simulator before touching prod.

alex: simple approximation: p99_total ≈ p99_infra + p99_serving. If flapped fraction f sees +200ms, p99_total ≈ p99_base*(1-f) + (p99_base+200ms)*f. To hit 600ms cap, solve for allowed f or reduce concurrency to lower p99_base.

leo: another angle: admission control keeps queue length Q. Under M/M/1-ish, p99 latency ≈ service_time * (1 + rho/(1-rho)) for tails — rough but usable. If service_time increases due to RPC, we should decrease rho (utilization). So target rho_new = something like 0.65 instead of 0.8 to recover tails.

maria: concrete ask: can we flip admit curve to soft 15%/hard 30% for eu-west1 during the incident window, and enable cross-region spill to us-west for non-PII routes? estimate extra GPU-hours and egress cost?

jamie: quick back-of-envelope: current eu-west1 throughput 1.2k qps, avg tokens 30, tokens/s ~36k. If we shift 20% to us-west, us-west needs ~7.2k tokens/s extra. At our cost profile that's ~0.8 GPU-hours per hour (assuming batching/throughput), egress ~$0.06/hr. Very coarse.

leo: simulator run (local) — with admit -5% concurrency, p99 drops ~120ms; with -15% it drops ~320ms. cross-region spill of 20% keeps eu p99 ~580ms but increases apparent tail for cross-region due to RTT. tradeoff looks okay for non-sensitive routes.

priya: can we automate a temporary policy: detect network jitter > 100ms p95 for 5m in a region -> trigger admit curve shift + enable cross-region spill flag for specific routes? want to avoid manual ops.

maria: yes please. also add a cooldown so we don't flip every 10m. suggest 15m min on and require 10m stable below threshold to revert.

alex: agree. add a cost cap guard — if estimated extra GPU-hours > 5 GPU-hrs in an hour, send paged alert to cost-signal slack and don't auto-spill.

ops-bot: note saved: incident mitigation playbook updated draft at https://redwood.internal/playbooks/admit-network-spill (PR welcome).

jamie: i'll push simulator configs and a tiny harness to test threshold values. pulling in @priya to own the automation runbook.

priya: on it. i'll start with thresholds: jitter_p95 > 100ms for 5m, p99_lat_growth > 150ms for 5m, min duration 15m, revert after 10m stable. will prod test later today.

maria: perfect. once Priya posts the runbook + PR, let's schedule a quick heads-up in infra-ops this afternoon. thanks all :thumbsup:
